Subject: Reranker integration - follow-up & eval questions

Hi Daniel — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery on the reranker / architecture side. Thanks again for walking us through the current search flow.

Recap (from call)
- Use case: product search + recommendations where current BM25 results are noisy for short queries.
- Volume: ~750k queries/day; peak 2.5k qps.
- Current infra: Postgres + Elastic for indexing; embeddings are precomputed offline today.
- Success metric: better relevance on manual eval set + lift in conversion (POC scope: improve top-5 relevance).

Topics we agreed to follow up on
1) Integration/SDK setup: auth model, sample SDK calls, and bundling into current API layer.
2) Routing & latency: options for synchronous rerank vs async enrich pipelines, and expected p95 for various top_k choices.
3) Structured output/tool calling: how to return scores, annotations, and downstream annotations for your microservice.
4) Embeddings & rerankers: model choices, dimension compatibility, and whether to use Redwood embeddings vs your own.
5) Evaluation plan: recommendations for metrics (nDCG@k, precision@k, MRR), and a simple sweep strategy for top_k and model size.

Attachments: I attached a high-level architecture diagram (reranker-arch.png) and a starter eval sheet (eval-metrics.xlsx) — please drop your eval set there if useful. Also sharing a Drive folder for scripts and examples: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-fastretail-eval

Proposed next steps
- You: drop a small sample of 200-500 query+gold items into the eval sheet (or tell us where to pull).
- Us: schedule a 30-min tech sync (Dylan + Ethan) to walk through SDK examples and the ranking API.
- Optional: we can run a quick 2-model comparison (lightweight reranker + BM25 baseline) on the sample set and return nDCG/precision numbers in 3-4 business days.

Are you available for a tech sync next week (Wed or Thu morning PT)?

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few quick questions from our engineering team so we can prep the eval slice before the tech call: 

1) Ranking API shape: do you accept the full candidate list and return a scored ordering, or do you only accept pairwise comparisons / score-by-id? We currently surface top-50 candidates from ES and would prefer a single-call rerank.

2) top_k tuning: what's the perf/latency tradeoff for top_k at 5/10/20? Our SLA target for search is p95 < 150ms if possible.

3) Embeddings: we currently use a 1536-d embedding produced offline. Is that dimension ok? Do you recommend switching to a different model/dim for reranking? Also, can we keep embeddings in our infra and send only candidate IDs to Redwood, or do you require embedding uploads to your store?

4) Cost model: ballpark token/call or per-request pricing for rerank calls (for sizing).

5) Security/compliance: we'll need SOC2/HIPAA posture info early in procurement. Is there a security contact or a packet we can get?

If you can answer those at a high level we can populate the eval sheet and confirm the tech sync.

Thanks Daniel — answers inline and a couple of recommended next steps. Looping in Dylan (solutions) and Ethan (runtime) for any deeper notes.

1) Ranking API shape
- Redwood supports list-based reranking: you send a single request with the query and candidate list (either raw text or candidate IDs with embeddings) and we return scored ranks. This aligns well with your flow that surfaces top-50 from ES.

2) top_k tuning & latency
- You can request a top_k or request scores for the full list and take the slice client-side. Default top_k we commonly use for evaluation is 10.
- Latency: p95 depends on model size and whether you pass embeddings or raw text. Typical p95 for a mid-size reranker (optimized runtime) at top_k=10 is ~80-160ms on dedicated infra; top_k=20 can add ~20–50ms depending on batching. We'll confirm on the tech call with Dylan/Ethan against your volume.

3) Embeddings/workflow
- 1536-d embeddings are fine. You can either:
  a) supply embeddings in the request (we score client-side without storing them), or
  b) upload/store embeddings in your private index and send candidate IDs (we'll fetch scores via secure private link).
- For evaluation it's easiest to send embeddings inline for the sample set to avoid indexing work.

4) Cost model
- We'll share a short cost spreadsheet; ballpark: rerank calls are priced per-request with tiered discounts at committed volume. We'll include a sample calc for the eval sample. Exact pricing goes through RevOps as usual.

5) Security/compliance
- I'll send you the SOC2 packet via a secure link; our security contact is security@redwood.inference. If you need an NDA or DPA, let me know and I can loop Legal.

Suggested next steps
- Please drop a 200–500 query sample and gold rankings into the eval sheet (or grant access), and indicate a preferred window for a 30-min tech sync.
- Dylan/Ethan: are you available Wed 12/09 or Thu 12/10 in the morning PT for the tech deep-dive?

Happy to sync —

Subject: Re: Reranker integration - follow-up & eval questions

Hey Daniel — Dylan here (solutions engineering). Wanted to add more concrete guidance so you can prep engineers and the eval slice. Apologies for the long note, but hopefully useful.

SDK & Auth
- SDKs: we have official SDKs (Python/Node) and a simple REST API. For a quick eval, the SDK's rerank client accepts: {"query": "...", "candidates": [...], "top_k": 10}.
- Auth: API keys for tests; production supports short-lived role-based tokens via our control plane (recommended for backend services). Keys are scoped per-environment.

API shapes (practical options)
1) Full-list rerank (recommended for you)
- POST /v1/rerank
- payload: {"query": "...", "candidates": [{"id": "c1", "text": "...", "embedding": [ ... ]}, ...], "top_k": 10, "return_scores": true}
- response: ranked list with score, explanation tokens if requested.

2) ID-only (embedding stored server-side)
- send candidate IDs, we fetch embeddings from your private store over a secure link; useful if candidates are large or you want to avoid payload size.

Embeddings and indexing
- 1536-d embeddings are supported. For production: we recommend keeping an index (FAISS/HNSW) close to your storage and using a hybrid approach: ES/approx search to surface candidates, then rerank via Redwood with inline embeddings for highest precision.

Batching & latency knobs
- Batch requests when throughput is high (we do automatic batching on the runtime).
- top_k tuning: evaluate top_k of [5,10,20] — for most retail search top-5/10 captures most business value; sweep with nDCG@5/10 and precision@5.
- If p95 latency is tight, consider: smaller top_k, a smaller reranker model, or a cached prefix for high-frequency queries.

Evaluation metrics & sweep suggestions
- Metrics: nDCG@5, nDCG@10, precision@5, MRR, and recall@50 for coverage.
- Sweep plan: run baseline BM25, run lightweight reranker (cheap model) and medium reranker (higher quality). For each, compute nDCG@5/10 and precision@5.
- Significance: bootstrap CI on nDCG; look for +0.03–0.05 nDCG as a meaningful lift depending on your baseline.

Example quick-start (Python pseudocode)
- from redwood import RedwoodClient
- client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
- resp = client.rerank(query="running shoes", candidates=[{"id":"p1","text":"...","embedding": [...]}, ...], top_k=10, return_scores=True)

Data & security notes
- For the eval sample, send anonymized IDs and remove PII.
- We support private deployments and VPC peering for customers that require no data egress; happy to discuss if needed for compliance.

I'll upload a short example script and a small sample curl request to the Drive folder (same link Marissa shared). If you grant our team access we can also drop a pre-populated eval sheet with formulas for nDCG/precision to make it plug-and-play.

If you want, I can take the lead on the tech sync and do a 20-min demo of the rerank call with your sample. Slot options: Wed 12/09 9:00–10:30 PT or Thu 12/10 9:00–11:30 PT.
